alt.en: The lower part of a printed page under the heading "GREEN SLEEVES.": a paragraph calling it a favourite tune "from the time of Elizabeth to the present day", two quotations from Shakespeare's Merry Wives of Windsor and one from Beaumont and Fletcher that name the tune, and a paragraph beginning "The earliest mention of the ballad of Green Sleeves in the Registers of the Stationers' Company is in September, 1580".
alt.es: La parte inferior de una página impresa bajo el encabezado "GREEN SLEEVES.": un párrafo que la llama una melodía favorita "from the time of Elizabeth to the present day", dos citas de Las alegres comadres de Windsor de Shakespeare y una de Beaumont y Fletcher que nombran la melodía, y un párrafo que empieza "The earliest mention of the ballad of Green Sleeves in the Registers of the Stationers' Company is in September, 1580".

caption.en: William Chappell's "Green Sleeves" in Popular Music of the Olden Time (London, 1855 to 1859), page 227, quoting the song's earliest record: "A new Northern Dittye of the Lady Greene Sleeves", entered by Richard Jones in the Stationers' register in September 1580.
caption.es: "Green Sleeves" de William Chappell en Popular Music of the Olden Time (Londres, 1855 a 1859), página 227, que cita el primer registro de la canción: "A new Northern Dittye of the Lady Greene Sleeves", inscrita por Richard Jones en el registro de la Stationers' Company en septiembre de 1580.

source: William Chappell, Popular Music of the Olden Time, vol. 1 (London: Cramer, Beale & Chappell, [1855 to 1859]), p. 227, "Green Sleeves" (detail: the section's opening, from its heading to the foot of the page)

alt.en: A printed page numbered 17, headed "Sonets and Histories, to sundrie new Tunes.": the end of an earlier poem signed "I. P.", then the italic heading "A new Courtly Sonet, of the Lady Green sleeues. To the new tune of Greensleeues.", the four-line refrain, and the first two stanzas, the first beginning "Alas my loue, ye do me wrong" under a large capital A decorated with flowers.
alt.es: Página impresa con el número 17 y el encabezado "Sonets and Histories, to sundrie new Tunes.": el final de un poema anterior firmado "I. P.", luego el título en cursiva "A new Courtly Sonet, of the Lady Green sleeues. To the new tune of Greensleeues.", el estribillo de cuatro versos y las dos primeras estrofas, la primera de las cuales empieza "Alas my loue, ye do me wrong" bajo una gran A mayúscula decorada con flores.

caption.en: "A new Courtly Sonet, of the Lady Green sleeues" as Edward Arber reprinted it in 1878 from A Handefull of Pleasant Delites (London, 1584), the earliest known printing of the words, with the refrain set above the first stanza.
caption.es: "A new Courtly Sonet, of the Lady Green sleeues" tal como Edward Arber lo reimprimió en 1878 a partir de A Handefull of Pleasant Delites (Londres, 1584), la primera impresión conocida de la letra, con el estribillo encima de la primera estrofa.

source: Clement Robinson and divers others, A Handful of Pleasant Delights (1584), edited by Edward Arber, English Scholar's Library No. 3 (London, 1878), p. 17, "A new Courtly Sonet, of the Lady Green sleeues"
library: University of Toronto, Robarts Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1878 (text of 1584); editor Edward Arber 1836-1912, Clement Robinson fl. 1566-1584 (Internet Archive record, which marks it NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT). Faithful scan of a flat page (see rights.md).

alt.en: A printed page numbered 230, headed "English Song and Ballad Music": a few lines of text, then the music "Tune of Green Sleeves. Oldest copy.", marked "Smoothly and in moderate time", in 6/8 on four pairs of staves with "Alas! my love, you do me wrong" and the refrain under the notes, and two more verses printed below.
alt.es: Página impresa con el número 230 y el encabezado "English Song and Ballad Music": unas líneas de texto y luego la música "Tune of Green Sleeves. Oldest copy.", marcada "Smoothly and in moderate time", en 6/8 en cuatro pares de pentagramas con "Alas! my love, you do me wrong" y el estribillo bajo las notas, y dos estrofas más impresas debajo.

caption.en: Page 230 of William Chappell's Popular Music of the Olden Time (London, 1855 to 1859): the "Oldest copy" of the tune, which he took from William Ballet's lute book, with G. A. Macfarren's harmony, the page our arrangement is read from.
caption.es: Página 230 de Popular Music of the Olden Time de William Chappell (Londres, 1855 a 1859): la "Oldest copy" (copia más antigua) de la melodía, que él tomó del libro de laúd de William Ballet, con la armonía de G. A. Macfarren, la página de la que parte nuestro arreglo.

source: William Chappell, Popular Music of the Olden Time, vol. 1 (London: Cramer, Beale & Chappell, [1855 to 1859]), p. 230, "Tune of Green Sleeves. Oldest copy."

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "XIV." and "What Child is this?", in four parts on two staves in 6/8, with the words "What Child is this, who, laid to rest, On Mary's lap is sleeping?" and the start of the chorus, "This, this is Christ the King", page number 32 at the foot.
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el encabezado "XIV." y "What Child is this?", a cuatro voces en dos pentagramas y en 6/8, con la letra "What Child is this, who, laid to rest, On Mary's lap is sleeping?" y el comienzo del estribillo, "This, this is Christ the King", y el número de página 32 al pie.

caption.en: No. XIV, "What Child is this?", in a printing of the 1870s of Bramley and Stainer's Christmas Carols New and Old (London, first series first published 1867): W. Chatterton Dix's Christmas words set to the Greensleeves tune.
caption.es: El n.º XIV, "What Child is this?", en una impresión de la década de 1870 de Christmas Carols New and Old de Bramley y Stainer (Londres, primera serie publicada por primera vez en 1867): la letra navideña de W. Chatterton Dix con la melodía de Greensleeves.
